"""Private synthetic-report publication with Entra authentication and no shared keys."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

from aegislake.scoring import verify_run

PUBLISH_FILES = ("report.html", "mitre.html", "report.json", "quality.json", "gold/alerts.json",
                 "attack-mapping.json", "dettect-techniques.yaml")


def publish(run_dir: Path, account: str, container: str = "reports") -> list[str]:
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9]{3,24}", account):
        raise ValueError("invalid Azure storage account name")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,61}[a-z0-9]", container) or "--" in container:
        raise ValueError("invalid Azure container name")
    manifest = verify_run(run_dir)
    if manifest["config"].get("synthetic") is not True:
        raise ValueError("only synthetic demonstration reports may be published by this command")
    # Lazy imports leave the local demo independent of Azure packages and credentials.
    from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential
    from azure.storage.blob import BlobServiceClient, ContentSettings

    credential = DefaultAzureCredential(exclude_interactive_browser_credential=True)
    uploaded = []
    try:
        with BlobServiceClient(f"https://{account}.blob.core.windows.net", credential=credential) as client:
            for relative in PUBLISH_FILES:
                path = run_dir / relative
                blob = f"{manifest['run_id']}/{relative}"
                mime = {".html": "text/html", ".yaml": "application/yaml"}.get(path.suffix, "application/json")
                with path.open("rb") as handle:
                    client.get_blob_client(container, blob).upload_blob(
                        handle, overwrite=True, content_settings=ContentSettings(content_type=mime)
                    )
                uploaded.append(blob)
            # Manifest is the commit marker, published only after all report uploads succeed.
            client.get_blob_client(container, f"{manifest['run_id']}/publication.json").upload_blob(
                json.dumps({"run_id": manifest["run_id"], "files": uploaded}),
                overwrite=True, content_settings=ContentSettings(content_type="application/json"),
            )
    finally:
        credential.close()
    return uploaded
src/aegislake/pipeline.py:
"""Reproducible immutable batch orchestration."""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import importlib.metadata
import json
import platform
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from aegislake import __version__
from aegislake.evaluation import metrics, population_stability_index, queue_mask, select_threshold
from aegislake.features import FEATURES, temporal_partitions
from aegislake.lake import file_sha256, ingest, write_json
from aegislake.models import Models, explain
from aegislake.report import render_report
from aegislake.review import alert_id


def run(
    source: Path, output: Path, *, train_days: int = 18, validation_days: int = 6,
    capacity: int = 25, seed: int = 42, synthetic: bool = False,
) -> Path:
    if capacity < 1:
        raise ValueError("capacity must be positive")
    config = {"train_days": train_days, "validation_days": validation_days,
              "capacity": capacity, "seed": seed, "synthetic": synthetic, "version": __version__}
    input_hash = file_sha256(source)
    identifier = hashlib.sha256((input_hash + json.dumps(config, sort_keys=True)).encode()).hexdigest()[:20]
    final = output / identifier
    if final.exists():
        from aegislake.scoring import verify_run

        manifest = verify_run(final)
        if manifest["input_sha256"] != input_hash:
            raise ValueError("run manifest mismatch")
        return final
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    staging = output / (identifier + ".partial")
    # Fail on overlapping run instead of concurrent writes or clobbering a failed checkpoint.
    staging.mkdir(exist_ok=False)
    try:
        events, quality = ingest(source, staging)
        if file_sha256(staging / "bronze" / "events.jsonl") != input_hash:
            raise ValueError("source changed during snapshot")
        train, validation, test = temporal_partitions(events, train_days, validation_days)
        if any(part["label"].isna().any() for part in (train, validation, test)):
            raise ValueError("benchmark requires labeled data; use the score command for future unlabeled batches")
        models = Models.fit(train, seed)
        validation_scores = models.score(validation)
        test_scores = models.score(test)
        validation_results, test_results = {}, {}
        for name, scores in validation_scores.items():
            threshold = select_threshold(validation, scores, capacity)
            validation_results[name] = metrics(validation, scores, threshold, capacity)
            test_results[name] = metrics(test, test_scores[name], threshold, capacity)
        champion = max(validation_results, key=lambda name: (
            validation_results[name]["f1"], validation_results[name]["precision"], name
        ))
        threshold = validation_results[champion]["threshold"]
        scores = test_scores[champion]
        selected = queue_mask(test, scores, threshold, capacity)
        alerts = []
        for position, (_, row) in enumerate(test.iterrows()):
            if not selected[position]:
                continue
            user, stamp = str(row["user"]), row["window_start"].isoformat()
            alerts.append({
                "alert_id": alert_id(user, stamp), "user": user, "window_start": stamp,
                "window_end": row["window_end"].isoformat(), "score": float(scores[position]),
                "model": champion, **explain(row),
            })
        alerts.sort(key=lambda item: (item["window_start"][:10], -item["score"], item["alert_id"]))
        gold = staging / "gold"
        gold.mkdir()
        for name, frame in (("train", train), ("validation", validation), ("test", test)):
            frame.to_parquet(gold / f"{name}_features.parquet", index=False)
        write_json(gold / "alerts.json", alerts)
        drift = {name: population_stability_index(train[name].to_numpy(), test[name].to_numpy()) for name in FEATURES}
        report = {
            "run_id": identifier, "champion": champion, "capacity": capacity,
            "validation": validation_results, "test": test_results, "feature_drift_diagnostics": drift,
            "quality": quality, "config": config, "features": FEATURES,
            "data_notice": (
                "SYNTHETIC DEMONSTRATION. Results measure a simulator and do not establish real-world detection."
                if synthetic else
                "LABELED OFFLINE DATA. Labels and collection scope limit generalization; review the data card."
            ),
            "split_boundaries": {
                "train_last_window_end": train["window_end"].max().isoformat(),
                "validation_first_window": validation["window_start"].min().isoformat(),
                "validation_last_window_end": validation["window_end"].max().isoformat(),
                "test_first_window": test["window_start"].min().isoformat(),
                "test_last_window_end": test["window_end"].max().isoformat(),
            },
        }
        render_report(staging, report, alerts)
        manifest = {
            "run_id": identifier, "input_sha256": input_hash, "config": config,
            "created_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(), "python": platform.python_version(),
            "packages": {name: importlib.metadata.version(name) for name in
                         ("duckdb", "numpy", "pandas", "pyarrow", "scikit-learn")},
            "artifacts": {
                path.relative_to(staging).as_posix(): file_sha256(path)
                for path in sorted(staging.rglob("*")) if path.is_file()
            },
        }
        write_json(staging / "manifest.json", manifest)
        staging.rename(final)
    except Exception:
        # Preserve failed staging for diagnosis. Never publish a partial run as successful.
        raise
    return final

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling>=1.26"]

name = "aegislake"
version = "0.1.2"
description = "Reproducible identity threat analytics with a security data lake and leakage-aware ML"
requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.14"
license = "MIT"
dependencies = [

  "numpy>=1.26,<3",
  "pandas>=2.2,<3",
  "pyarrow>=21,<25",

]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["pytest>=8.3,<10", "pytest-cov>=6,<8", "ruff>=0.11,<1", "pip-audit>=2.9,<3", "pyyaml>=6.0.2,<7"]

[project.scripts]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]

.github/workflows/ci.yml:
name: Quality and reproducible demo
on:
  push:
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python: ["3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5.6.0
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
      - name: Install project and checks
        run: |
          python -m venv .venv
          .venv/bin/python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel
          .venv/bin/python -m pip install ".[dev,azure]"
          echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: Lint
        run: ruff check src tests scripts
      - name: Unit and end-to-end tests
        run: pytest --cov=aegislake --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=xml
      - name: Dependency vulnerability scan
        run: pip-audit --progress-spinner off
      - name: Generate recruiter demo and exact environment record
        run: |
          aegislake demo --output runs
          python -m pip freeze > runs/environment.txt
      - name: Upload synthetic outputs
        if: matrix.python == '3.12'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4.6.2
        with:
          name: aegislake-synthetic-demo
          path: |
            runs/**/report.html
            runs/**/mitre.html
            runs/**/attack-mapping.json
            runs/**/dettect-techniques.yaml
            runs/**/report.json
            runs/**/manifest.json
            runs/environment.txt
            coverage.xml
          retention-days: 14
          if-no-files-found: error
  infrastructure:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Compile Bicep without signing in or deploying
        run: az bicep build --file infra/main.bicep --stdout > /tmp/aegislake-template.json
      - name: Build non-root container
        run: docker build --tag aegislake:ci .
      - name: Run container as its non-root user
        run: docker run --rm aegislake:ci demo --days 15 --users 12 --train-days 9 --validation-days 3

"""ATT&CK mapping semantics and DeTT&CT YAML interoperability."""

import copy
import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

from aegislake.attack import describe_mapping, dettect_administration, write_attack_exports, yaml_text


class AttackTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_candidate_tactics_are_deduplicated_catalog_memberships(self):
        mapped = describe_mapping(["T1078", "T1078", "T1110.003"])
        self.assertEqual(mapped["status"], "hypothesis")
        self.assertEqual(len(mapped["techniques"]), 2)
        valid = next(item for item in mapped["techniques"] if item["technique_id"] == "T1078")
        self.assertEqual({item["tactic_id"] for item in valid["candidate_tactics"]},
                         {"TA0001", "TA0003", "TA0004", "TA0005"})
        self.assertNotIn("TA0008", str(valid))
        spray = next(item for item in mapped["techniques"] if item["technique_id"] == "T1110.003")
        self.assertEqual(spray["candidate_tactics"], [{"tactic_id": "TA0006", "tactic_name": "Credential Access"}])

    def test_unknown_ids_are_preserved_without_invented_tactics(self):
        mapped = describe_mapping(["T9999", "T9999"])
        self.assertEqual(mapped["techniques"], [])
        self.assertEqual(mapped["unmapped_technique_ids"], ["T9999"])
        self.assertEqual(describe_mapping([])["techniques"], [])

    def test_deployment_template_does_not_invent_operational_scores(self):
        template = dettect_administration()
        self.assertEqual(template["version"], 1.2)
        self.assertEqual(template["file_type"], "technique-administration")
        self.assertEqual(template["domain"], "enterprise-attack")
        for technique in template["techniques"]:
            detection, visibility = technique["detection"][0], technique["visibility"][0]
            self.assertEqual(detection["location"], [])
            self.assertEqual(detection["score_logbook"][0]["score"], -1)
            self.assertEqual(visibility["score_logbook"][0]["score"], 0)
            self.assertIsNone(detection["score_logbook"][0]["date"])
            self.assertFalse(visibility["score_logbook"][0]["auto_generated"])
            self.assertIn("Unassessed SOC", detection["applicable_to"][0])

    def test_yaml_loads_as_the_expected_administration_structure(self):
        template = dettect_administration()
        self.assertEqual(yaml.safe_load(yaml_text(template)), template)
        special = {"notes": "quotes: \"ok\"\nUnicode: áé and # comments", "flags": [True, None, 0], "empty": []}
        self.assertEqual(yaml.safe_load(yaml_text(special)), special)

    def test_export_counts_unique_windows_and_keeps_mapping_provenance(self):
        report = {"run_id": "test-run", "data_notice": "SYNTHETIC"}
        alerts = [{"alert_id": "a1", "user": "do-not-export-this-user", "source": "private-source",
                   "attack_hypotheses": ["T1078", "T1078", "T1110.003"]},
                  {"alert_id": "a2", "attack_hypotheses": []}]
        before = copy.deepcopy(alerts)
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            root = Path(directory)
            write_attack_exports(root, report, alerts)
            text = (root / "attack-mapping.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            exported = json.loads(text)
            self.assertEqual(exported["technique_counts"], {"T1078": 1, "T1110.003": 1})
            self.assertEqual(len(exported["alerts"]), 2)
            self.assertEqual(exported["alerts"][0]["alert_id"], "a1")
            self.assertNotIn("do-not-export-this-user", text)
            self.assertNotIn("private-source", text)
            self.assertEqual(yaml.safe_load((root / "dettect-techniques.yaml").read_text()),
                             dettect_administration())
        self.assertEqual(alerts, before)

    def test_empty_export_still_offers_a_reviewable_inventory(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            root = Path(directory)
            write_attack_exports(root, {"run_id": "empty", "data_notice": "SYNTHETIC"}, [])
            exported = json.loads((root / "attack-mapping.json").read_text())
            self.assertEqual(exported["technique_counts"], {"T1110.003": 0, "T1078": 0})
            self.assertEqual(exported["alerts"], [])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import json

import pandas as pd
import pytest

from aegislake.azure import publish
from aegislake.pipeline import run
from aegislake.scoring import score, verify_run


def test_end_to_end_manifest_splits_and_idempotency(completed_run):
    source, path = completed_run
    manifest = verify_run(path)
    assert {"mitre.html", "attack-mapping.json", "dettect-techniques.yaml"} <= manifest["artifacts"].keys()
    report = json.loads((path / "report.json").read_text())
    assert report["quality"]["duplicates"] == 1
    assert report["quality"]["rejected"] == 1
    assert "SYNTHETIC" in report["data_notice"]
    train = pd.read_parquet(path / "gold/train_features.parquet")
    validation = pd.read_parquet(path / "gold/validation_features.parquet")
    test = pd.read_parquet(path / "gold/test_features.parquet")
    assert train["window_end"].max() <= validation["window_start"].min()
    assert validation["window_end"].max() <= test["window_start"].min()
    for result in report["test"].values():
        assert result["daily_alerts_max"] <= 12
    assert run(source, path.parent, **{key: manifest["config"][key] for key in
               ("train_days", "validation_days", "capacity", "seed", "synthetic")}) == path


def test_tampered_artifact_is_rejected(completed_run, tmp_path):
    import shutil

    _, path = completed_run
    copy = tmp_path / "copy"
    shutil.copytree(path, copy)
    (copy / "quality.json").write_text("{}")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="integrity"):
        verify_run(copy)


def test_cloud_destination_and_real_data_publication_guard(completed_run, tmp_path):
    import shutil

    _, path = completed_run
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="account"):
        publish(path, "https://evil.example")
    copy = tmp_path / "real"
    shutil.copytree(path, copy)
    manifest = json.loads((copy / "manifest.json").read_text())
    manifest["config"]["synthetic"] = False
    (copy / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="only synthetic"):
        publish(copy, "aegisexample")


def test_unlabeled_future_scoring_has_no_evaluation_metrics(completed_run, event, tmp_path):
    _, reference = completed_run
    source = tmp_path / "future.jsonl"
    source.write_text(json.dumps(event | {
        "timestamp": "2026-02-10T10:01:00Z", "label": None,
    }) + "\n")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="domain-shift"):
        score(reference, source, tmp_path / "refused")
    destination = score(reference, source, tmp_path / "scored", allow_domain_shift=True)
    result = json.loads((destination / "scoring.json").read_text())
    assert result["windows"] == 1
    assert result["metrics"] is None


@pytest.mark.parametrize("fail_yaml", [False, True])
def test_cloud_publication_keeps_linked_exports_and_commits_last(completed_run, monkeypatch, fail_yaml):
    import azure.identity
    import azure.storage.blob

    from aegislake.azure import PUBLISH_FILES

    _, path = completed_run
    uploads = []
    closed = []

    class Credential:
        def close(self):
            closed.append(True)

    class Blob:
        def __init__(self, name):
            self.name = name

        def upload_blob(self, payload, *, overwrite, content_settings):
            if fail_yaml and self.name.endswith(".yaml"):
                raise RuntimeError("simulated upload failure")
            data = payload.read() if hasattr(payload, "read") else payload
            uploads.append((self.name, data, content_settings.content_type))

    class Client:
        def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
            pass

        def __enter__(self):
            return self

        def __exit__(self, *args):
            pass

        def get_blob_client(self, container, name):
            return Blob(name)

    monkeypatch.setattr(azure.identity, "DefaultAzureCredential", lambda **kwargs: Credential())
    monkeypatch.setattr(azure.storage.blob, "BlobServiceClient", Client)
    if fail_yaml:
        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="simulated"):
            publish(path, "aegisexample")
        assert not any(name.endswith("publication.json") for name, _, _ in uploads)
    else:
        published = publish(path, "aegisexample")
        assert len(published) == len(PUBLISH_FILES)
        assert uploads[-1][0].endswith("publication.json")
        assert json.loads(uploads[-1][1])["files"] == published
        assert any(name.endswith("mitre.html") and mime == "text/html" for name, _, mime in uploads)
        assert any(name.endswith("dettect-techniques.yaml") and mime == "application/yaml"
                   for name, _, mime in uploads)
        assert any(name.endswith("attack-mapping.json") and mime == "application/json"
                   for name, _, mime in uploads)
    assert closed == [True]

# AegisLake

**Identity threat analytics: security data engineering, reproducible machine learning, and human-led investigation.**

A portfolio project by Carlo Alessandro Cabrera. AegisLake turns authentication events into a small security data lake, compares detection methods under an analyst workload budget, and produces an offline investigation dashboard.

> Verified synthetic demo: 32 tests pass with 87% measured coverage; dependency audit, Bicep build, and non-root Docker execution pass. [Execution evidence](https://github.com/krlokbrera/aegislake/actions/runs/41215188019). Live Azure deployment remains pending.

[Spanish guide](docs/GUIA_ES.md) · [Research and design](docs/RESEARCH_ES.md) · [Azure](docs/AZURE.md) · [Model card](docs/MODEL_CARD.md) · [Data card](docs/DATA_CARD.md) · [Interview walkthrough](docs/CV_AND_INTERVIEW_ES.md)

## Why this project

A suspicious login is useful only if an analyst can investigate it. This project treats detection as a data product: reliable ingestion, explicit data contracts, temporal evaluation, traceable evidence, and bounded review workload. It combines the data engineering and cybersecurity experience that a generic classification notebook usually separates.

| Capability | Implemented evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Data engineering | Bronze snapshot, validated silver Parquet partitions, SQL feature aggregation, gold outputs |
| Analytics | Daily SOC KPIs, quality reconciliation, feature drift diagnostics, offline report |
| Applied AI | Rules, Isolation Forest, logistic regression, hybrid score, validation-only model selection |
| ML evaluation | Train/validation/test by time; average precision; precision/recall; false positives; daily capacity |
| Security | Keyed pseudonymization, no model pickle loading, private Blob access, no keys in code |
| Human oversight | Evidence summaries and a local append-only-at-application-level review ledger |
| Azure engineering | Bicep, optional finite Container Apps Job, managed identity, scoped RBAC |
| Delivery | Python package and CLI, Docker, tests, GitHub Actions, source-backed design documentation |

## Run the local demo

Python 3.11 or 3.12 is recommended. Run from the repository root:

```bash
python -m venv .venv
# Windows PowerShell:
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
# Linux/macOS: source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install ".[dev]"
aegislake demo --output runs
```

The CLI prints the completed run directory. Open its `report.html` in your browser. It is a self-contained, offline dashboard with workload charts, model comparisons, searchable evidence and paginated alerts. Open the linked `mitre.html` page to explore the curated ATT&CK map and jump to alerts filtered by technique. Keep the HTML pages and their `attack-mapping.json` and `dettect-techniques.yaml` downloads together. Alerts expose candidate tactic IDs as well as technique IDs. [DeTT&CT integration and scoring scope](docs/DETTCT_ES.md).

Default workload: 30 days, 50 identities, seed 42, 18 training days, six validation days, six test days, and at most 25 queued user windows per test day. These are simulator settings, not organization-wide capacity recommendations.

```bash
pytest --cov=aegislake --cov-report=term-missing
ruff check src tests scripts
pip-audit --progress-spinner off
```

For Docker:

```bash
docker build -t aegislake:local .
docker run --rm -v aegis-demo:/app/runs aegislake:local
# The named volume retains output; copy it using a separate read-only container if needed.
```

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Synthetic JSONL or canonical labeled export"] --> B["Bronze snapshot and quality checks"]
    B --> C["Silver Parquet by UTC date"]
    B --> Q["Rejected line references"]
    C --> D["Closed 15-minute SQL windows"]
    D --> E["Temporal evaluation and model selection"]
    E --> F["Gold alert queue and offline report"]
    F --> G["Analyst review ledger"]
    F --> H["Private Azure reports"]
```

The reference implementation is single-node batch processing. It does not claim streaming delivery guarantees, distributed exactly-once processing, or incident response automation.

## Useful commands

```bash
# Evaluate your canonical labeled dataset:
aegislake run --input data/labeled-events.jsonl --output runs --train-days 18 --validation-days 6

# Record a review; replace the run path and alert identifier:
aegislake review --run runs/RUN_ID --alert-id ALERT_ID --decision needs_context --reviewer analyst-01

# Adapt an existing Graph JSON export after setting AEGIS_PSEUDONYM_KEY privately:
aegislake adapt-entra --input data/graph-export.json --output data/pseudonymous.jsonl

# Score future unlabeled events from an integrity-checked reference:
aegislake score --reference runs/RUN_ID --input data/future.jsonl --output runs/future-batch

# Upload only synthetic reports after Azure login and scoped RBAC setup:
python -m pip install ".[azure]"
aegislake publish --run runs/RUN_ID --account YOUR_STORAGE_ACCOUNT
```

Synthetic-trained references require an explicit `--allow-domain-shift` for new-batch scoring. This is an experimental interoperability path, not validation on Entra telemetry.

## Outputs

Each completed run contains:

- `bronze/events.jsonl`: original snapshot, kept locally.
- `silver/event_date=.../events.parquet`: validated partitions.
- `quarantine/rejected.json` and `quality.json`: disposition accounting.
- `gold/*_features.parquet`: train, validation and test windows.
- `gold/alerts.json`: evidence queue without ground-truth labels.
- `report.html`, `mitre.html` and `report.json`: investigation dashboard, curated technique explorer, results and limitations.
- `manifest.json`: input hash, configuration, versions and output hashes.
- `reviews.sqlite`: created when an analyst records a decision.

Raw telemetry and outputs are ignored by Git. GitHub Actions uploads only synthetic reports, manifests, coverage and an environment record.

## Verification evidence and remaining scope

Read [VALIDATION_STATUS.md](docs/VALIDATION_STATUS.md) for observed checks and remaining limits. [A generated synthetic report](examples/demo/report.html), its JSON metrics and manifest are included for inspection. Azure student access and live deployment are pending.

## License

MIT for original project code. External datasets retain their own terms and attribution requirements. No employer or client data is included.

# Verificación del frontend

El informe offline utiliza dos páginas: `report.html` para métricas e investigación y `mitre.html`
para técnicas, tácticas candidatas y el traspaso de evaluación a DeTT&CT. Los archivos descargables
`attack-mapping.json` y `dettect-techniques.yaml` deben conservarse junto a las páginas.

## Comportamiento comprobado en navegador

- Búsqueda por identidad: la muestra seed-7 devuelve cuatro ventanas para employee-0043.
- Búsqueda sin coincidencias: estado vacío y paginación desactivada.
- Paginación: ocho alertas por página, con segunda página 9–16 de 146.
- Filtro T1078: cinco ventanas, todas con esa hipótesis.
- Orden temporal descendente y evidencias desplegables.
- Selección de técnica en MITRE y navegación a la cola filtrada correspondiente.
- Marco móvil de 390 px: ambas páginas sin desbordamiento horizontal del documento.
- Contenido y estilos integrados sin CDN, fuentes externas, analítica o peticiones de datos.

Las pruebas unitarias comprueban escape de HTML, preservación de métricas, recuentos por ventana,
estados vacíos, conservación de técnicas desconocidas y estructura del YAML. La integración
comprueba manifiestos y la publicación de todos los archivos enlazados antes del marcador cloud.

La muestra publicada se regenera con puntuaciones completas; no depende de la extracción de tarjetas
HTML utilizada para la primera revisión local. Los resultados describen datos sintéticos.

Consulta [el registro de ejecución](VALIDATION_STATUS.md) para los resultados medidos de CI y
[la guía DeTT&CT](DETTCT_ES.md) para el significado de las exportaciones y puntuaciones iniciales.

# Mapeo SOC/SIEM con ATT&CK y DeTT&CT

AegisLake relaciona sus señales de identidad con dos técnicas: **T1110.003 Password Spraying** y
**T1078 Valid Accounts**. Cada técnica contiene sus tácticas candidatas con identificador y nombre,
los campos necesarios y la referencia oficial. El catálogo vive en `src/aegislake/attack.py` y se
reutiliza en las alertas de evaluación, las de scoring de lotes nuevos y el informe visual.

| Técnica | Tácticas asociadas en el catálogo consultado | Señal implementada |
| --- | --- | --- |
| T1110.003 | TA0006 Credential Access | Fanout de al menos 8 identidades por fuente y tasa de fallos de al menos 50 % |
| T1078 | TA0001 Initial Access; TA0003 Persistence; TA0004 Privilege Escalation; TA0005 Stealth | Al menos 4 destinos por identidad en una ventana cerrada de 15 minutos |

Las tácticas son pertenencias del catálogo: una alerta con T1078 **no demuestra** que hayan ocurrido
persistencia, elevación de privilegios o todos los objetivos asociados. El fanout por sí solo tampoco
demuestra movimiento lateral; por eso no se añade una táctica de movimiento lateral a esa señal.

La semántica de la señal y sus falsos positivos posibles están visibles en la página MITRE. La página
muestra una selección de identidad de cinco columnas, no una medida de cobertura de toda la matriz.
Los nombres se comprobaron el **31 de octubre de 2026**; TA0005 aparece como Stealth en las fuentes
consultadas. Las versiones antiguas pueden mostrar Defense Evasion. El catálogo no se actualiza en red.

## Qué aporta DeTT&CT

DeTT&CT es un proyecto de Rabobank CDC que utiliza ATT&CK para administrar fuentes de datos, visibilidad
y capacidad de detección. No es un clasificador de alertas y su puntuación no equivale al score de ML.
Una técnica puede generar muchas alertas de simulación y seguir careciendo de evidencia de cobertura
operativa en una organización.

Cada ejecución de evaluación genera dos archivos adicionales, enlazados desde `mitre.html`:

- `attack-mapping.json`: evidencia por identificador de alerta, técnica, tácticas candidatas y campos
  canónicos requeridos. No duplica nombres de usuarios o direcciones de origen. Conserva técnicas
  desconocidas como no mapeadas. Cuenta cada ventana una vez por técnica; los recuentos pueden solaparse.
- `dettect-techniques.yaml`: plantilla de administración de técnicas v1.2 para una implantación SOC aún
  no evaluada. Se utiliza `file_type: technique-administration`, según el ejemplo oficial del proyecto.

El YAML conserva **detección -1** (ninguna detección desplegada registrada) y **visibilidad 0** (ninguna
visibilidad operativa registrada). Son valores iniciales conservadores de una plantilla sin evaluación,
no una afirmación de que tu SOC real carezca de controles. No se inventa una fecha de despliegue, una
ubicación de regla SIEM ni una puntuación positiva. Antes de utilizarla operativamente, el responsable
debe editar el ámbito, plataformas, fuentes y calidad de datos, localización de las reglas, comentarios
y logbook de puntuaciones con evidencia de su entorno.

El alcance `Unassessed SOC deployment (AegisLake candidate)` mantiene esa plantilla separada de una
evaluación de activos reales. `platform: all` es un valor de compatibilidad de la plantilla: no acredita
que el detector funcione en todas las plataformas. Debe ajustarse antes de generar una capa operacional.

## Flujo de uso

1. Ejecuta `aegislake demo --output runs` o una evaluación sobre datos etiquetados autorizados.
2. En `mitre.html`, selecciona una técnica, lee su regla y revisa las alertas enlazadas.
3. Descarga el YAML y el JSON. Los archivos también están en el directorio de la ejecución.
4. Abre el YAML en el editor de DeTT&CT y sustituye la plantilla por una evaluación documentada del SOC.
5. Con una instalación de DeTT&CT revisada y compatible con la versión de ATT&CK utilizada, genera sus
   capas para Navigator. Ejemplo del CLI oficial: `python dettect.py d -ft dettect-techniques.yaml -l`.
6. Versiona la evaluación y conserva evidencia de pruebas de reglas y de la calidad de los datos.

Mientras el YAML mantenga los valores iniciales -1/0, la visualización de cobertura de DeTT&CT no debe
interpretarse como un heatmap de detecciones acreditadas. El informe AegisLake muestra volumen de
hipótesis; DeTT&CT administra capacidad evaluada. No se convierten entre sí mediante una fórmula.

La exportación se contrasta con el ejemplo oficial de administración y se comprueba con un parser YAML.
Esto valida estructura y semántica propia, no la ejecución completa del CLI externo ni la eficacia en
un SIEM real. No se añaden credenciales o conectores de un SOC ni se envían datos a servicios externos.

## Fuentes primarias

- [DeTT&CT: repositorio y propósito](https://github.com/rabobank-cdc/DeTTECT)
- [Administración de técnicas](https://github.com/rabobank-cdc/DeTTECT/wiki/YAML-administration-techniques)
- [Ejemplo oficial v1.2](https://github.com/rabobank-cdc/DeTTECT/blob/master/sample-data/techniques-administration-endpoints.yaml)
- [Puntuación de detección](https://github.com/rabobank-cdc/DeTTECT/wiki/Detection-scoring)
- [Puntuación de visibilidad](https://github.com/rabobank-cdc/DeTTECT/wiki/Visibility-scoring)
- [MITRE: Password Spraying](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/003/)
- [MITRE: Valid Accounts](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/)
- [MITRE: tácticas Enterprise](https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/enterprise/)
